examples.ko: 서커스 단원이 공중에서 곡예를 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The circus performer showed acrobatics in the air.
The children clapped in amazement at the acrobatics.
The motorcycle stunt show was really nerve-racking.

examples.ko: 곡예 운전을 하는 차 때문에 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled by a car driving recklessly.

examples.ko: 곡예가 끝나자 관객들이 일어서서 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: When the acrobatics ended, the audience stood and applauded.

examples.ko: 곡예처럼 위험한 운전은 절대 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must never drive dangerously like it's a stunt.

explain: 서커스처럼 몸으로 하는 아슬아슬한 재주를 말해요. 일상에서는 '곡예 운전'처럼 위험하게 움직일 때 비유로도 써요. 발음은 쓰인 대로가 아니라 [고계]예요.
explain_en: It refers to daring physical skills like those at a circus. In daily life it is also used figuratively for risky movement, as in '곡예 운전' (stunt-like driving). It is pronounced [고계], not as spelled.

examples.en: The idols' group dance was truly perfect.
Migratory birds perform a group dance in the sky.

examples.ko: 열 명이 함께 추는 군무가 멋있었어요.
examples.en: The group dance performed by ten people was cool.

examples.ko: 군무 연습 때문에 매일 늦게까지 남아요.
examples.en: I stay late every day because of group dance practice.
In a ballet ensemble dance, the dancers have to be in sync.
This song is famous for its group choreography.

explain: 여러 사람이 함께 추는 춤을 말하고, 혼자 추는 '독무'의 반대예요. 아이돌 춤이 정확하게 맞으면 '칼군무'라고 많이 말해요. 새 떼나 물고기 떼가 한꺼번에 움직이는 모습을 '군무'에 비유하기도 해요.
explain_en: It means a dance performed by many people together, the opposite of '독무' (a solo dance). When an idol group's moves match precisely, people often say '칼군무'. Flocks of birds or schools of fish moving together are also compared to a 군무.

examples.ko: 이 악보에는 도돌이표가 두 개 있어요.
examples.en: This sheet music has two repeat signs.

examples.ko: 도돌이표를 만나면 앞으로 돌아가서 다시 연주해요.
examples.en: When you meet a repeat sign, you go back and play again.

examples.ko: 선생님이 도돌이표 부분을 한 번 더 치라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher told me to play the repeated section once more.

examples.ko: 도돌이표를 못 봐서 중간에 끝내 버렸어요.
examples.en: I didn't see the repeat sign and ended in the middle.
Every meeting is like a loop, and it's frustrating.
My days repeat the same, like a loop.

explain: 악보에서 앞부분으로 돌아가 다시 연주하라고 알려 주는 기호예요. 요즘은 같은 일이나 말이 끝없이 되풀이될 때 '도돌이표 같다'고도 해요.

phrases.en: Our conversations always go around in circles.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 이야기나 상황이 끝없이 되풀이되어 답답할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the same topic or situation repeats endlessly and feels frustrating.

explain_en: This is the sign in sheet music telling you to go back and play a section again. Today people also say '도돌이표 같다' when the same things or words repeat endlessly.

examples.en: A batter came up in the bottom of the ninth with the bases loaded.
A grand slam was hit, and the stadium got fired up.
The pitcher got through the bases-loaded jam well.
When the bases were loaded, the whole crowd stood up.

examples.ko: 저는 만루에서 삼진을 당하는 장면이 제일 아쉬워요.
examples.en: The most disappointing thing for me is a strikeout with the bases loaded.
The team lost after missing a bases-loaded chance.

explain: 야구에서 1루, 2루, 3루에 모두 주자가 있는 상황을 말해요. '만루 홈런', '만루 위기', '만루 찬스'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여 자주 써요. 소리는 [말루]로 나요.
explain_en: In baseball, it means runners are on first, second and third base all at once. It is often placed before other words, as in '만루 홈런', '만루 위기' and '만루 찬스'. It is pronounced [말루].

examples.en: I play the bassoon in the orchestra.
The sound of the bassoon is low and soft.

examples.ko: 동생이 학교 밴드에서 바순을 배우고 있어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is learning the bassoon in the school band.
In this piece, the bassoon carries the melody.
The bassoon is much bigger than the clarinet.
I want to become a bassoonist.

explain: 낮고 부드러운 소리를 내는 목관악기예요. '바순을 불다' 또는 '바순을 연주하다'라고 말해요. 오케스트라나 관악 합주에서 낮은 음을 맡을 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It is a woodwind instrument with a low, soft sound. You say '바순을 불다' or '바순을 연주하다'. In orchestras and wind ensembles it often covers the low parts.

examples.en: He sang a serenade beneath her window.

examples.ko: 이 곡은 모차르트의 세레나데 중에서 가장 유명해요.
examples.en: This piece is the most famous of Mozart's serenades.
A serenade concert is held in the park in the evening.
I prepared a serenade for my love confession.

examples.ko: 세레나데는 밤에 연인에게 불러 주는 노래예요.
examples.en: A serenade is a song you sing to your lover at night.

examples.ko: 기타 반주에 맞춰 세레나데를 연습하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm practicing a serenade to a guitar accompaniment.

explain: 밤에 연인에게 불러 주는 노래를 뜻하기도 하고, 클래식에서는 '소야곡'이라고도 하는 곡 종류를 가리켜요. 일상 대화보다는 음악 이야기나 낭만적인 장면에서 주로 써요.
explain_en: It can mean a song sung to a lover at night, and in classical music it is a type of piece also called '소야곡'. You hear it more in talk about music or romantic scenes than in everyday conversation.
